claims.claim: Independent Reuters reporting on Nokia's Q2 2026 results corroborated the material AI/cloud demand signal: comparable operating profit rose 18% to EUR 434 million, AI/cloud sales doubled to EUR 446 million, Q2 AI/cloud orders were EUR 2.8 billion, and Nokia raised its full-year comparable operating-profit outlook to EUR 2.1-2.6 billion.

risks.risk: Independent reporting still reflects company-reported quarter data; it corroborates the reported results and demand context but does not independently audit the underlying accounting records.

contradictions.contradiction: The prior issuer evidence records comparable margin improvement alongside negative reported margin from restructuring; this Reuters source corroborates comparable-profit strength but does not independently resolve the comparable-versus-reported accounting distinction.

unknowns.unknown: Durability of AI/cloud order conversion beyond the current capacity-constrained build cycle remains unproven.

claims.claim: Reuters independently reported that Nokia's Q2 2026 net sales of EUR 4.82 billion beat expectations and that the company raised full-year comparable operating-profit guidance to EUR 2.1-2.6 billion while AI/cloud sales doubled, providing an independent execution/expectations checkpoint against the existing issuer-only lineage.

risks.risk: A raised annual outlook can still be missed if AI/cloud order conversion, component availability, or restructuring execution deteriorates later in 2026.

unknowns.unknown: Post-Q2 realized margins and cash restructuring costs require later-period validation.
